settings.introHTML: This lesson teaches you how to make and answer phone calls in French, including asking for and giving telephone and mobile numbers. You will practise typical telephone phrases such as allô, C'est bien le... ?, and Je me suis trompé(e) de numéro, while also learning how French phone numbers are organised and spoken in pairs.
settings.informationHTML:
After completing this unit, you will be able to:

  • Ask for and give a telephone or mobile number in French.
  • Recognise and respond to common telephone expressions for checking, correcting, and ending a call politely.
  • Understand the main French landline and mobile prefixes and how numbers are grouped when spoken aloud.
  • Use bien to confirm information in expressions such as C'est bien ça.
  • Pronounce the numbers cinq, six, sept, huit, neuf, and dix more confidently in connected speech.

dialogues.informationTextHTML: This section introduces short telephone exchanges for asking for a number, checking a number, correcting mistakes, and arranging to meet.

phraseTable1.informationTextHTML: Read each line, then play the audio to hear how the number is spoken in two-digit groups.
phrases: Quel est ton numéro de portable ?
Quel est votre numéro de téléphone, s'il vous plaît Madame ?
What's your phone number please, Madam?

phraseTable2.informationTextHTML: Listen for how speakers confirm a number, apologise, and end the call politely when there has been a mistake.
phrases: Hello Madam, this is 01 23 08 09 15, isn't it?
Ah non, je suis désolée, il y a une erreur ! C'est le 01 23 08 08 16.
Oh no, I'm sorry, there's a mistake. This is 01 23 08 08 16.

phraseTable3.informationTextHTML: Notice how speakers identify themselves, ask for someone, and move from the phone call to arranging to meet later.
phrases: André est là, s'il vous plaît ?
André, tu veux prendre un verre avec moi ce soir ?
André, do you want to have a drink with me this evening?
Oui, je veux bien. À quelle heure ?
Yes, I'd like that. At what time?

vocabulary.informationTextHTML: This section introduces the core vocabulary used for telephone calls, checking numbers, apologising, and ending a call politely.

You will learn:

  • Key telephone nouns such as numéro, portable, and téléphone fixe.
  • Useful telephone expressions such as allô, C'est moi, and À plus tard.
  • How to apologise and point out a mistake — such as désolé(e), erreur, and se tromper de.
phrases: to make a mistake / to be mistaken about something
Je me suis trompé(e) de numéro.
I've made a mistake about the number.
You've made a mistake about the number.
Vous vous êtes trompé(e) de numéro.
You've made a mistake about the number.

instructionsLayout.paragraphHTML: This section explains how French telephone numbers are grouped and how bien can be used to confirm that information is correct.

grammar1.informationTextHTML: This section introduces the main French landline regions, the mobile prefixes 06 and 07, and the habit of saying numbers in pairs. Hover over a region on the map or in the key to see where that area code is used, then click to hear the code.

grammar2.informationTextHTML: This section shows how bien can help speakers check or confirm information on the telephone.

pronunciation1.informationTextHTML: In this part, focus on the basic pronunciation of the numbers five to ten. Listen carefully and repeat each word aloud.

pronunciation2.informationTextHTML: Here, focus on how six, huit, and dix change depending on whether the next word begins with a consonant or a vowel.

instructionsLayout.paragraphHTML: This section gives you a chance to practise the key points from this unit. You will check your ability to give and confirm phone numbers using bien, choose the correct typical phone phrases for everyday calls, and respond to short listening tasks set in a French phone conversation.

typedTransformExercise1.informationTextHTML: Listen to each audio clip and type the phone number you hear. Keep the digits in two-digit groups. Use Check answers to review your entries, Show answers for support, and Reset to practise again.

inlineChoiceGroup1.instructionsText: Listen to each exchange and choose the correct word or form.
inlineChoiceGroup1.informationTextHTML: Listen carefully and complete each telephone exchange with the correct option. Use Check answers to review your choices, Show answers for support, and Reset to try again.

items.text: Ah non, Monsieur, je suis [désolé|*désolée]. Il y a [un|*une] erreur ! C'est [*le|la] 02 25 09 10 47.
Ah non, Madame, je suis [*désolée|désolées]. Il y a une [horreur|*erreur] ! C'est [*le|les] 03 26 09 13 47.

selectExercise2.instructionsText: Listen to the dialogue and choose the correct reply each time.
selectExercise2.informationTextHTML: Complete the telephone conversation by choosing the correct spoken reply at each step. Work through the dialogue, then use Check answers to review it, Show answers for support, and Reset to try again.
